title: He invented the DNA sequencing method that made a $200 human genome possible. It just won him a Wolf Prize.

sources.text: NewsBytes - Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Mayer awarded 2026 Wolf Prize in Chemistry
New India Abroad - India-born scientist Shankar Balasubramanian wins 2026 Wolf Chemistry Prize

caption:
He invented the DNA sequencing method that made a $200 human genome possible. It just won him a Wolf Prize.

The Chennai-born chemist, now at the University of Cambridge, was recognized for inventing the Solexa/Illumina next-generation DNA sequencing method - the technology behind most of the world's genomic sequencing today.

Their method helped make genome sequencing cheap and fast enough for everyday precision medicine - work that started in a lab, not a hospital, but ended up reshaping how diseases get diagnosed and treated worldwide.

Balasubramanian's invention didn't just win him a prize - it became invisible infrastructure underneath a huge share of modern genomic medicine.
